en.why: The text sits one layer behind the product, and the product covers about 1/3 of the wordmark, which creates a front layer and a back layer. The sentence breaks in the middle and the device becomes part of it, so the eye travels from the left word through the screen to the right word. Translation is shown through occlusion: the word goes in as black source text and comes out as gradient-colored translation, with no arrows.
spec: Film 11s with hard cuts at 3.2s and 7.8s. Wordmark-rise scene 0–3.2s: product lights 0–1.15s, sinks while the wordmark rises 0.9–2.7s (1.8s, 54 frames). Pass-through scene 3.2–7.8s: source text slides in 1.0s (30 frames; 3.75–4.75s and 5.85–6.85s), translation emerges 0.4s (12 frames; 4.75–5.15s and 6.85–7.25s). Slot-in scene 7.8–11.0s: device drops in 8.55–9.05s (0.5s, 15 frames), light ring glows 9.05–9.65s (0.6s, 18 frames)

Wordmark rise, device drop, translation emerging and lockup cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1) (expo.out); source text slide linear; product lighting power2.inOut; word lighting and ring glow power2.out and power2.inOut

Fixed perspective camera, 20° fov, distance 34 units, medium close-up. When the wordmark rises, the case sinks from top 350px to 515px (165px, about 15% of frame height) while the wordmark rises 255px; slow drift: case scale +2.5% in the first scene, earbud scale +2% in the second

Layer order: text at the back, 3D product in the middle, text in front. In the pass-through scene the translation is clipped to start at the earbud tip (x 1060px) and the source text is hidden past x 820px; in the slot-in scene the sentence splits into two groups with a 400px gap, one earbud wide, and the left words light first (8.05s), the right words second (8.3s)

The light ring turns on after both word groups have lit and the device has dropped in (9.05s); the translation emerges at the earbud's sound outlet (tip at 1060px, 580px) and its language label follows 0.12s later

Black background in the first and last scene, light gray #f5f5f7 in the middle one; wordmark vertical gradient #ff5a0a → #ff7a26 → #ffb27a → #ffd2ad (Archivo Black 340px), translation gradient #4b2dff → #9b33ff → #ff2f8a (background-clip: text), sentence words #5e5e63 lighting to #f5f5f7
en.prompt: Build a front-and-back interleave of text and product called Text–Object Interleave as an 11-second film with three scenes and hard cuts at 3.2s and 7.8s. Use three layers: text at the back, your 3D product in the middle (fixed perspective camera, 20° fov, distance 34 units), text in front. Scene 1 (black stage): the case lights up (rim 0–0.45s, key 0.25–1.15s), then from 0.9 to 2.7s it sinks 165px (about 15% of frame height) with expo.out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) while a large wordmark with a vertical orange gradient (#ff5a0a to #ffd2ad) rises 255px from behind its top edge and is clipped at the bottom. Scene 2 (light gray #f5f5f7): an earbud close-up with its sound outlet fixed on screen; source text slides at constant speed (linear) for 1.0s into the earbud and is hidden, then 0.4s later the translation emerges from the outlet with expo.out in a purple-pink gradient (#4b2dff to #ff2f8a, background-clip: text); run two passes (3.75–5.15s and 5.85–7.25s). Scene 3 (black): a sentence split into two word groups with a 400px gap one earbud wide; the left words light first (8.05s), the right words 0.25s later; the earbud drops into the gap from above over 0.5s with expo.out (8.55–9.05s), then its light ring glows over 0.6s (9.05–9.65s) and the wordmark settles in with expo.out. Use layered HTML + GSAP over a Three.js canvas.
says: The text rises up from behind the product
A phone slides down between two pieces of text
The text passes through the earbuds and comes out in another language
vs: Word-by-Word Highlight controls reading pace on plain text; Text–Object Interleave puts text and object into an occlusion relationship.
Dispense Line-up has objects slide out of the main subject in turn, synced word by word with the caption; Text–Object Interleave emphasizes the front-and-back layering of text and object.

en.title: Text–Object Interleave: Example and Code Recipe
en.description: Type rises from behind a product, an earbud slots into a sentence and a word passes through it as a translation. Make it with Claude Code or Codex.
en.lede: Text and object interleave in depth: type rises from behind the product, a device slots into a gap in a sentence, or a word passes through an object and comes out as another word.
en.name: Text–Object Interleave

body.h2: How to make a Text–Object Interleave with Claude Code or Codex
body.body:
Order the layers back to front: text, 3D product, text. In the first scene (0–3.2s) the product sinks 165px while the wordmark rises 255px over 1.8s with expo.out, cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), so the product covers about a third of the wordmark. Use a fixed 20° fov camera at 34 units.

In the pass-through scene (3.2–7.8s) the source text slides in linearly over 1.0s and is hidden past x 820px, while the translation is clipped to start at the earbud tip (x 1060px) and emerges in 0.4s. In the slot-in scene (7.8–11.0s) the sentence splits with a 400px gap, one earbud wide, the device drops in over 0.5s and a light ring glows 0.6s later.

Press the copy button to send this recipe to Claude Code or Codex, or install the skill once with npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard. The agent builds the three scenes with the 3D product between two text layers. Render an MP4 with HyperFrames, or port the GSAP timeline to your website.

en.alt: A white earbud passing in front of the pink word こんにちは under the heading Live Translation.
faq: What is a text behind object effect?

It places type on a layer behind the main subject so the subject partly covers the letters, which gives a flat title a front and a back. This film also lets a word pass through an object and slots a device into a sentence.
How does the film show a translation without arrows?
The object marks the change. The word enters the earbud as black source text and leaves it as gradient-colored translation clipped at the earbud tip, and a language label follows 0.12s later.

body.h2: 用 Claude Code 或 Codex 做文字穿插实物效果
body.body:
图层从后到前依次是：文字、3D 产品、文字。第一幕（0–3.2s）里产品下沉 165px，字标用 1.8s 上升 255px，缓动 expo.out（cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)），产品遮住字标约三分之一。相机固定，视场角 20°，距离 34 个单位。

穿过场景（3.2–7.8s）中，原文用 1.0s 线性滑入，越过 x 820px 的部分被隐藏；译文从耳机尖端（x 1060px）起裁切，用 0.4s 出现。插入场景（7.8–11.0s）里，句子从中间拉开 400px，宽度正好是一只耳机，设备用 0.5s 落入，之后光环亮起 0.6s。

点击复制按钮，把配方发给 Claude Code 或 Codex，也可以用 npx skills add krisyangdev/motionboard 安装 skill。agent 会做出这三个场景，让 3D 产品夹在两层文字之间。可以用 HyperFrames 渲染成 MP4，也可以把 GSAP 时间线移植到网站上。

faq: 什么是文字在物体后面的效果？
把文字放在主体后面的图层，主体盖住一部分字，平面标题就有了前后层次。这支片子还让文字穿过实物，并让设备插进句子中间。
片子怎么表现翻译，又没有箭头？
靠实物本身标记变化。文字以黑色原文进入耳机，从耳机尖端以渐变色译文出来，语言标签晚 0.12s 跟上。
